1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line spacing, though letter spacing appears default rather than visibly generous.

2.why: Instructions such as 'Enter your registered details...' use sentence case with no italics, no all-caps, and no dense text blocks (the uppercase 'NORTHSTAR BANK' is only the brand mark).

3.why: The provided screenshots are desktop-width (1280px) with a narrow centered card, so readability at an actual mobile screen size is not demonstrated.

4.why: Instructions are one to two short plain sentences, e.g. 'Enter the six-digit code sent to your phone. The code expires in 10 minutes.'

5.why: The phone field shows an example placeholder '+447700900000', but the six-digit identity code field offers no example of the expected input format.

6.why: No screen contains more than two short lines of instructional text, so no long block must be read to proceed.

7.why: Only manual typing into the code field is observed, and no copy buttons or affordances for codes or secrets appear in any screenshot.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry is visible in any of the five provided screens.

9.why: Standard single-line inputs are used, but no explicit indication of browser autofill or password-manager support can be confirmed from the screenshots.

10.why: Each screen shows a 'Step X of 3' indicator, a bold heading, and a single high-contrast primary button ('Continue', 'Verify and continue').

11.why: Each screen centres on one primary action, though a secondary 'Use different details' link is also present on the verification screens.

12.why: Progressing from step 1 to 2 clearly states a code was sent and what to do next, but after a failed attempt the system only says 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.'

13.why: Retry after an error is invited and the entered code is retained, but no re-request/resend code option and no reveal/hide control are visible anywhere.

14.why: The error message 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.' does not blame the user but fails to state the actual problem or a specific fix.

15.why: No reading time limit or countdown is shown, but the screens explicitly state 'The code expires in 10 minutes', imposing a moderate time limit on code entry.
